# dsh-knowspace
**Agent-native, local-first knowledge infrastructure for DeepSeekHarness.**
English | 简体中文

> **Status: Work in progress · Public placeholder · No public alpha release**
> Last README update:
October 12, 2026. Development continues in a private repository. This public repository currently se
rves as the project's official landing page; it does not provide an installable plugin or publicly a
uditable source code.
`dsh-knowspace` aims to make personal knowledge available to both people and authorized AI agents wi
thout making a cloud service, a vector database, or an always-on AI process the owner of that knowle
dge. It is designed as a DeepSeekHarness plugin, not a separate knowledge server.
The long-term goal is a shared foundation for notes, retrieval, rendering, and interaction that othe
r agents, Skills, scripts, and domain-specific plugins can reuse.
## Why KnowSpace?
Most AI workflows treat knowledge as one-off chat context or an external retrieval service. KnowSpac
e takes a different approach:
- **Your files are the source of truth.** Markdown notes and images remain ordinary, portable local

assets.
- **Agents work within permissions.** Access is scoped by workspace and user policy; knowled

ge is not silently exposed to every agent.
- **Offline comes first.** Reading, editing, and baseline

search should work without network access.
- **Sync is optional.** A WebDAV endpoint can exchange s

upported knowledge assets between devices without hosting a separate KnowSpace service.
- **Interact
ive content is reusable infrastructure.** Math rendering, diagrams, temporary pages, and input colle
ction belong in common capabilities rather than being reinvented by every Skill.
**Design principle:** Your knowledge, your control. AI participation should be explicit, scoped, and
nciple:** Your knowledge, your control. AI participation should be explicit, scoped, and reviewable.
## Project status
The first five internal development rounds have been recorded as closed in the private project's pro
gress history. **This is not equivalent to completing public release acceptance.** Some implementati
on results have been reported internally, while important security, synchronization, and end-to-end
checks remain part of the acceptance plan.
| Area | Current description | Public availability |
| DeepSeekHarness Host/Client integration and sidebar | Implemented in private development records;

compatibility is version-sensitive | Not released |
| Local workspaces, Markdown, JPG/PNG assets, ba

sic search | Implemented/reported internally; subject to regression checks | Not released |
| Agent
knowledge tools, edits, and change previews | Implemented/reported internally; end-to-end gateway ch

ecks are tracked separately | Not released |
| Markdown and mathematical notation | Existing private

implementation and test history; maintained rather than rewritten | Not released |
| WebDAV bidirec
tional synchronization | Designed and worked on internally; cross-device/conflict/data-safety eviden

ce must satisfy release gates | Not released |
| Interactive HTML, drawing input, submission bridge
| Partially implemented or planned; security sandbox and real UI flows are not yet fully accepted |

Not released |
| Editable knowledge diagrams and advanced local retrieval | Architecture decisions m
ade; integration and acceptance are pending | Not released |
**No installation instructions are published yet.** A pinned, reproducible installation process and
compatibility matrix will accompany the first usable alpha release. Please do not treat a developmen
t design or an example tool name as a supported public API.
## Product capabilities and direction
### 1. Knowledge: workspaces, files, and optional sync
Two intended workspace modes keep their responsibilities separate:
| Workspace | Behavior |
| **Local** | Independent knowledge workspace stored on the current device; never synced automatical

ly. |
| **Synced** | Complete local working copy with optional, bidirectional WebDAV synchronization
when connectivity is available. |
Markdown is the primary portable knowledge format. The default **sync allowlist** is `.md`, `.jpg`,
and `.png`; PDF, video, audio, 3D files, executable content, and native diagram sources are not auto
matically uploaded as originals. Rich media may remain local. A Markdown document explicitly derived
from rich media is an independent knowledge asset, not a continuously attached copy of its source.
The design prioritizes change history, understandable diffs, collision protection, non-destructive c
onflict handling, and recovery over silent overwrites.
### 2. Retrieval: local-first search and evidence
KnowSpace starts with workspace-aware textual retrieval. Its planned search improvements borrow *ide
as* from Greb-style candidate retrieval and ranking, but **do not use a cloud Greb API or make any t
hird-party MCP service mandatory**.

## Privacy and safety boundaries
- No silent model calls, note summarization, or behavioral profiling while browsing, indexing, or sy

ncing.
- Agent-readable workspace scopes are distinct from private or explicitly agent-denied worksp

aces.
- Agent writes and interactive submissions must be tied to valid authorization; unknown actor

identity must not turn into permissive access.
- File changes, conflicts, and failure states should

be inspectable and recoverable.
- Synchronization must not silently upload local-only source media,

`.drawio`, or arbitrary executable files.
- New retrieval and diagram integrations must not replace
the established storage/sync protocol without explicit review and migration tests.
These are **design and release requirements**. They should not be interpreted as claims that every s
ecurity scenario has already passed independent audit.
